description:
How will Christ satisfy his people when they see him face to face? Wesam Saad resumes the question left at the previous meeting and explores the joy of personal fellowship with Jesus on the renewed earth. He emphasises that Christ himself desires his people to behold his glory. The hope is physical and relational: believers will enjoy the presence of the same Jesus whom the disciples knew, with his glory revealed.

Saad then considers loving Christ without the obstruction of sin. A glorified body removes that barrier, while growing knowledge of an infinite Lord means that enjoyment need not become exhausted. He distinguishes the lasting importance of present faithfulness from continuing growth in eternity, acknowledging that he cannot explain every aspect of their relationship. His emphasis is on increasingly knowing, loving and delighting in Christ rather than eventually knowing everything.

Direct worship provides a further dimension of this joy. Saad pictures redeemed people praising Christ together, while marking his proposed pattern of weekly gatherings as his interpretation. The closing discussion turns expectation into present practice: seeking Christ through his word and prayer, encouraging fellow believers, resisting temptation and enduring difficulty with renewed hope. Indirect worship is introduced for the next meeting.

questions.question: What does Jesus’ prayer reveal about believers seeing his glory?
questions.answer: Saad stresses that this is Christ’s own desire, not merely something believers want from him. He connects the request to the Father’s love for the Son and to Christ’s redeeming work. The anticipated encounter is therefore described as something Jesus welcomes, rather than a reluctant audience with a distant ruler.

questions.question: What does the study mean by enjoying Christ’s bodily presence?
questions.answer: Saad expects real fellowship with the God-man on a renewed earth, rather than existence as a bodiless soul. He uses walking, talking and sharing time with Jesus to illustrate that relational hope. These illustrations express personal access and affection; they are not a timetable of individually guaranteed future events.

questions.question: How will the removal of sin affect loving Christ?
questions.answer: Saad says that remaining sinful desires presently hinder wholehearted love and enjoyment of Christ. He expects the glorified body to be free from that obstruction. His point is not that Jesus must become more worthy of love, but that the believer’s response will no longer be impeded by sin.

questions.question: Why will continued learning about Christ not end in boredom?
questions.answer: Christ is infinite, while his people remain finite. Saad argues that knowing him more can therefore continue to deepen love and enjoyment without making believers all-knowing. Full enjoyment according to a person’s capacity does not mean possessing the full extent of everything there is to know about Christ.

questions.question: How does Saad relate present faithfulness to growth in eternity?
questions.answer: He maintains that present service and endurance for Christ have lasting consequences, while also affirming future growth in knowledge and enjoyment. When asked how these relate, he acknowledges that he cannot account for all the factors. The study should therefore not be read as claiming that all growth stops at death or as supplying a precise formula for future capacities.

questions.question: How does the scene in Revelation 5 help explain direct worship?
questions.answer: Saad uses the multitudes praising the Lamb as a picture of the joy of worship directed to Christ in his presence. He explicitly distinguishes that passage’s setting from the eternal state, then suggests that such shared praise can help listeners imagine future worship. He does not present the passage as though it directly describes every detail of his proposed eternal gathering.

questions.question: How certain is the proposed weekly gathering in the New Jerusalem?
questions.answer: Saad presents it as his interpretation, drawing on Isaiah 66 and considering continuity between the millennial kingdom and the eternal state. He explicitly says the proposal is not firmly established. Details such as the weekly pattern and means of travel therefore remain possibilities in his discussion, not settled promises supplied by the study.

questions.question: What present responses are encouraged by this hope?
questions.answer: The closing discussion encourages attention to Christ through Scripture and prayer, helping other believers draw near to him, and valuing him above tempting alternatives. Participants also connect future joy with endurance through sorrow and difficulty. Saad welcomes these applications as ways of letting hope shape daily faithfulness.
